reviewNote: Help review the content: facts, design concepts, examples, and translations. Initial translations still await independent fluent review. Automated checks do not replace expert or language review.
indexSubtitle: One mechanic at a time. Explore animations, tuning checks, and the choices behind a good encounter.
purposeText: Bosses can look different yet ask the player to solve the same problem. This atlas separates a fight into mechanics and shows how to make each one readable, distinct, and resilient to player upgrades.
siteMapIntro: Open a lesson from the beginning or jump directly to the part you need.
mechanicsNavText: All published mechanics, one lesson per page.
simulationNavText: Animations show attack phases, threat geometry, and different outcomes.
conceptsNavText: Reusable design concepts and patterns behind each mechanic.
examplesNavText: Concrete 2D and 3D bosses with focused video clips.
sourcesNavText: Talks, articles, accessibility guidelines, and technical documentation.
contributeNavText: Check facts, concepts, examples, and translations or add a mechanic.
soon: The atlas starts with Charge. Help us add the next mechanic.
contributeText: Suggest a mechanic, check a fact or design concept, improve an explanation, or review a translation. Every page lives in the public repository.
conceptsIntro: These are practical lenses for analysis, not a universal classification. Use them to explain why a charge works and what to test.
examplesIntro: Compare the cue, commitment, danger area, arena, and recovery. A reference is a design example, not a ready-made recipe.
watchVideo: Watch the boss fight on YouTube
sourceNote: The diagram is an original teaching example. These talks, articles, guidelines, and technical references cover boss structure, attack phases, cues, accessibility, and collision implementation.
